memory_update.text: ONTO should remain on the HBM stack process watchlist as a relatively direct US-listed inspection/metrology exposure, especially after Dragonfly G5 HBM4 selection evidence.

KLIC is a lower-attention HBM process-equipment candidate because of first HBM system shipment, FTC, vertical wire, and hybrid-bonding exposure; survival depends on follow-on production-order evidence.
CAMT belongs in the inspection/metrology lane for advanced packaging and HBM-related yield control, but needs tighter verification of HBM-specific revenue versus broader advanced-packaging demand.

For this node, separate direct HBM stack-process tools from broader substrate/2.5D/OSAT capacity; Amkor is a reference capacity asset, while ONTO/KLIC/CAMT are closer to process-control or process-tool bottlenecks.

US-listed pure-play materials suppliers for HBM underfill, temporary bonding/debonding chemistry, and ultra-thin wafer handling remain sparse; later passes should search OTC/ADR and Japan/Korea/Taiwan listings separately.

node: HBM stack process and advanced-packaging workflow: die thinning, vertical interconnects, bonding, underfill, inspection, and co-packaging with accelerators
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the HBM stack and advanced-packaging workflow finds the cleanest US-listed discovery lane in process-control and assembly-equipment suppliers rather than HBM producers. The strongest underfollowed candidates are Onto Innovation for HBM inspection/metrology, Camtek for advanced-packaging inspection/metrology, and Kulicke & Soffa for thermocompression, hybrid-bonding, vertical-wire, and memory interconnect tools. Amkor is included as a larger reference/overflow-capacity anchor for outsourced advanced packaging and test, not as a pure HBM-stack process supplier. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
